title: T1587.002 — Develop Capabilities - Code Signing Certificates
subtitle: Watch the life of a self-signed certificate from both sides: the attacker builds trust out of nothing, and the SOC turns that trust into a detection.
aria: Animated diagram: an attacker invents a company name, generates a self-signed code signing certificate, stamps the certificate fields, signs a backdoor, delivers it to a victim, and the SOC blocks the thumbprint, sweeps endpoints for files signed by that certificate, and shares indicators with malware repositories.

steps.caption: te: a company that does not exist, or a real software company copied letter for letter. Nothing is registered anywhere. The identity will exist only inside the certificate file. nothing to detect yet. This step leaves no public record, which is what makes the self-signed path cheap
steps.defender: Source, CI and artifact logs record who changed what and which artifact was published.

steps.title: This is the effect the official description
steps.caption: names: users and security tools may trust a signed file more than an unsigned one even when they do not know the issuer. Filters score signed files lower, allow rules match on "is signed", and users read the company name and click. If the plan needs full chain trust, a second step installs the attacker's root certificate (T1553.004). public popularity says nothing here. Watch signer rarity inside your own estate instead
